lens: Documentation adherence — P9 no-sprawl + DOC-CATALOG + doc-class + thin-gateway
answer: PR #12 lands docs/decisions/ADR-0117-repo-hygiene-gitignore-audit-config-and-kyverno-consolidation.md but FAILS to register the new ADR into ANY of the canonical indexes. ADR-INDEX.md still says 'Next ADR number: 0110' and contains no row for ADR-0117 (or for 0110-0116). DOC-CATALOG.md has zero rows referencing ADR-0117 — and the existing pattern (doc.adr_0096..doc.adr_0099) shows per-ADR rows are the established convention for individually-cataloged ADRs. CHANGELOG.md has no 2026-05-16 entry for this PR. The two machine-readable mirrors (decisions.json, catalog.json) have no ADR-0117 entries. The ADR file itself partially conforms to TPL-ADR but has structural defects: (1) frontmatter omits canonical fields (`id`, `title`, `bominal_source`) and uses a non-template ad-hoc schema (`deciders`, `purpose`); (2) `related: []` is empty despite the ADR explicitly discussing kyverno (must cite ADR-0039), Argo GitOps (must cite ADR-0040/ADR-0041), and sitting adjacent to supply-chain admission policy — violates cite-the-rule discipline; (3) no `## Sunset / Reversal` section (the template's mandatory closure for terminal vs forward-pointing ADRs); (4) `## Status` is duplicated (once in frontmatter `status: Accepted`, once as bottom section); (5) Naming-Justification section exists but does NOT use the canonical NAME/JUSTIFICATION code-block format from the template. This is a multi-doc DOC-CATALOG drift event: a new ADR was minted, merged, but never wired into the catalog substrate the rest of the doc machinery reads. Future readers querying ADR-INDEX.md or machine-readable/decisions.json will not see ADR-0117 exists. The 'Next ADR number: 0110' stale pointer means any subsequent ADR author will collide on 0110 instead of advancing to 0118.
